corvane-depot-night-noise-report.pdf:
# 1. Summary

Night-time noise at Sallowfield Terrace is dominated by tonal reversing alarms and by refrigeration units left running on parked trailers. The LAmax from reversing alarms reached 78 dB at the nearest NSR, well above the 60 dB used by the council as a sleep disturbance threshold. With broadband alarms, relocated trailer bays and a 3 m earth bund, we predict LAmax values of 59 dB or below, which would support the extended hours.

# 3. Survey method

Measurements followed Larkspur measurement procedure MP-3. The sound level meter was mounted on a tripod 1.5 m above ground, at least 3.5 m from any reflecting surface other than the ground, and fitted with a windshield. Readings were discarded for any period in which the wind speed at the microphone exceeded 5 m/s or rain fell.

The logger stood at the rear fence of 11 Sallowfield Terrace (position S1) for five weeknights. Attended readings were taken 10 m from a reversing tractor unit and 5 m from a refrigeration unit (position S2). Logger files were saved as corvane_s1_night1.csv to corvane_s1_night5.csv.

Readings from the Tessaly SL-55 are traceable to a laboratory calibration certificate held on our project file, and the field calibration check made before and after each session drifted by less than 0.3 dB.

# 8. Limitations

This report describes sound levels measured at the positions and during the periods stated. It does not predict levels for other weather, operating conditions or site layouts, and it should not be relied on by anyone other than the client named in it without the written agreement of Larkspur Acoustics.

pellow-mill-facade-report.docx:
## 1. Summary

Freight trains on the Wendlecombe branch line set the façade design for the west elevation. Night-time pass-bys reached 87 dB LAmax at the second-floor west façade. Bedrooms on that elevation need glazing of at least Rw 41 dB and acoustic trickle ventilators, or mechanical ventilation so that windows can stay closed. The south and east elevations need only standard thermal double glazing.

## 3. Survey method

Measurements followed Larkspur measurement procedure MP-3. The sound level meter was mounted on a tripod 1.5 m above ground, at least 3.5 m from any reflecting surface other than the ground, and fitted with a windshield. Readings were discarded for any period in which the wind speed at the microphone exceeded 5 m/s or rain fell.

Loggers ran for 72 hours on the second-floor scaffold of the west elevation (position W2) and at first-floor level on the south elevation (position S1). Fourteen freight pass-bys were identified at night from the audio files pellow_w2_audio_01.wav to pellow_w2_audio_14.wav.

Readings from the Brakel NX3 are traceable to a laboratory calibration certificate held on our project file, and the field calibration check made before and after each session drifted by less than 0.3 dB.

# 7. Limitations

This report describes sound levels measured at the positions and during the periods stated. It does not predict levels for other weather, operating conditions or site layouts, and it should not be relied on by anyone other than the client named in it without the written agreement of Larkspur Acoustics.

# 8. Data handling statement

Larkspur Acoustics keeps raw audio recordings and logger files for six years after a report is issued and then deletes them. Recordings that capture speech are stored encrypted and are not shared outside the project team. A client may ask for a copy of the data behind any figure in this report.
